barCharacter: Liam de Lioncourt, the same bar as rounds 1 and 2. He is the over-formal aesthete whose elevated register is the joke and who keeps exposing himself without noticing, which is Quill's comic job. The corpus has only seven lines Liam speaks, so his 12 are those lines plus the narration about him and the player lines aimed at him.

ours: Why I, of all who stand before thee, plumed and polished, hopeful, glinting in the lamplight? Height.
Easily. My helm alone cost a fortune, from the finest bucket maker in Kent.
A wince. I have been winced at by a queen.
I challenged the little red clerk who underlineth my words to a duel. He underlined the challenge.
Thou art a rose. I know not what thou art.
O lady of the singing box, who granteth wishes after midnight like a well, I wish thee.
Crumb, a tin hearth with a sulking loaf in it, is the only suitor who is also breakfast.
Remember me, if thou rememberest aught, as tall.
{losses} ladies chose another. Each, I am certain, under duress.
Prince is truly royal, fair one. I know, for I have paid his processing fee. It is processing.
Wed, by a parson who hath been dead some years, which is irregular, but he was free.
Thou all-beholding wedge, behold my back.
bar: Maybe doing a 180 degree spin from cliches is good, but embracing cliches is like... making a 360 degree spin from them! So disruptive!
You! Save me from the consequences of my actions! Suggest an idea that lives up to my own hype!
Ugh- I have no reason to care about this, but suddenly it's all I care about! Someone stop this madness!
Please, friend, help me find an unpopular band to worship until pop culture inevitably ruins it.
Yes, we have indeed encountered a culinary block. Perhaps you can suggest something appropriately artistic?
But I was sighing deeply because I couldn't help but think: supposing I were to actually acquire such a machine, I wonder...where in time would I go?
What kind of status could I post that would be idiot-proof?
Narrator: a hipster vampire whose stand-offish demeanor hid that he was truly a lovable dork.
Narrator: Liam vanishes in a cloud of mist and angst.
Narrator: Later, you see Liam beaming to himself. Liam? Beaming?
Player option: 3.85 billion BC, so you can be into existing before it was cool.
Player option: Well, I guess I'll be going then, because there's no way anyone could ever be as cool as Liam.
headToHead.voiceJudgement: Ours. With the names covered, the 12 could only be Quill, and not just because of thee and thou: the long build that collapses onto one plain word ('...glinting in the lamplight? Height.'), the apostrophe that ends on a broken wish ('...like a well, I wish thee.'), and the ten-syllable jab ('Thou all-beholding wedge, behold my back.'). Strip the archaic words and these still could not be Dash, Nav or Crumb. Two of Liam's seven spoken lines ('What kind of status could I post...', 'Ugh- I have no reason to care...') could be Vera or Polly.
headToHead.constructionJudgement: Ours, on the 12. The round 2 gap is closed: Quill now exposes himself without knowing it. The boast carries its own proof, and the proof gives him away: 'finest bucket maker in Kent', 'winced at by a queen', 'under duress', 'He underlined the challenge'. That is Liam's 360 move, done more economically. Each line turns on its last one to four words and none explains itself. Liam's advantage is that he hands the player a want in the same sentence. Quill's 12 do that only once ('which side are we on' is not among them). Across the bank the construction is weaker, which is where the biggest gap below comes from.
headToHead.quotableJudgement: Tie. 'I have been winced at by a queen.', 'Thou art a rose. I know not what thou art.', 'Height.' and the little red clerk stand alone as clips and describe a type of person, as Liam's 'save me from the consequences of my actions' and the 360 do. But four of our 12 need the room to land: the bucket maker needs the helm on screen, 'It is processing' needs Prince's brief, and Crumb and the wedge need their targets. Liam's best two travel with no context at all. Even overall, on all three counts, which on this bar's rule goes to ours, narrowly. The margin lives in the best 12, not in the bank.

genericLines: O thou, before whose beauty candles gutter, is this seat taken? [stock pickup line used as the button; the oldest turn there is]
Whoever calleth thee cute. Lambs are cute. Thou art a plague year, fair one, in the best sense. ['in the best sense' is a modern stock tag that explains the backhand; second 'lamb' in the bank]
A muse should sit still and be described. This one keepeth answering back. I have lost my place. [the last sentence admits the problem, which the persona bans]
My odes await the right muse to end them. That is why. That is the only why. [explains the secret; 'That is the only why' winks at the audience]
I was once read aloud at a royal wedding. I have finished a poem. [states the secret outright as the lie; the viewer is told, not left to work it out]
Choose me, and all thy virtues I shall prove. In sixteen hundred, that rhymed with love. [explains its own joke and states the age, which the persona bans]
No contest. {rival} hath never been in a ballad. Nor, strictly, have I, but I have read several. [a second sentence that admits it; the persona bans exactly this]
In matters of the heart, as of the hat, I am inclined to feathers. Thou shalt never lack feathers. [no turn; he wears a bucket helm with no hat and no feathers]
I hold a grudge forever. Point it at thine enemies and it becometh loyalty. Name them. [swappable: Vex or Crumb could say it; stock 'your flaw is really a strength' reframe]

Thou art the first to send me home. Today. [stock 'Today.' button]
A smile. At me. Not the helm, I checked behind me. At me. [stock 'is that for me? (looks behind)' gag, in a modern register]

templates: The button fragment ('Full statement. Clipped one-to-four-word button.'): 26 of 112 lines. Examples: 'Bound in calfskin.', 'There were four.', 'Quickly, too.', 'He also doeth hair.', 'Any horse.', 'Like an animal.', 'Poor lamb.', 'Name them.', 'Ask it.', 'She said goats.', 'Learn thy trade.', 'It is processing.', 'Line one.', 'Again, please.', 'My left.', 'Today.' Overall, 72 of 112 lines are stacks of short declaratives. This is a stand-up's tag rhythm, not the persona's stated main shape.

My verse is unbearably long: 7 lines. Norman Conquest preamble, acrostic 'pray thy name is long', 'a great deal of sonnet', ode of four hundred lines, 'short reply... four cantos', 'I read to thee... Quickly, too', 'reading aloud at table'.

Duels: 6 lines (mispronounce, {rival} accepted, comma, little red clerk, forty duels, 'Chosen, and I challenged no one'). The persona says 'rarely'. Each turns on something specific, so only the count is a problem.
Dead date or era as the punchline: Restoration, 1637, 1644, sixteen hundred, Norman Conquest, Michaelmas, plague year. 'Plague' appears 3 times and 'lamb' twice.
Recite a rival's secret from the brief (goats, the old slice, never been read, the door farewell): 4 lines. These are the wingman and roast slots where Quill stops sounding like Quill.
ruleBreaks: Hard rules are clean. No line is over its limit (openers top out at 12/12, jabs at 10/10, answers and twists at 20/20: 'Having beheld thee ninety seconds...', 'I apologise now for challenging thy friend...', 'Madam, whose thousand copper roads...', 'Crumb hath kept a slot warm...'). No em dashes, emoji, asterisks or stage directions. No 'as an AI', therapy talk, real person or brand. Nothing goes past PG-13: bleeding, the gibbet, the pillory and 'thou shalt die young' are dark but fine.

Look contradicted. The CAST look is a bucket helm, tabard and cape. 'She laughed at my ruff. The ruff hath been dismissed without a reference.' gives him a ruff he does not have. 'In matters of the heart, as of the hat, I am inclined to feathers.' gives him a hat and feathers.

Persona ban on admitting it: 'Nor, strictly, have I, but I have read several.', 'I have lost my place.', 'I am still standing in the field.', 'I have finished a poem.' (this states the secret outright).
Persona ban on stating the age: 'In sixteen hundred, that rhymed with love.'

Persona ban on lists of three: 'Fetch the court painter. Fetch any painter. Fetch whoever painted the inn sign.', 'Lo, I am fair, and bored, and thou art furniture.', 'Much admired. Briefly. Then worth an onion.'
The iamb of offence is not kept on a cut. 'Remember me, if thou rememberest aught, as tall.' runs about 12 syllables, not ten (the line is great; trim it to scan or accept the break knowingly).
Register slips into modern idiom: 'in the best sense', 'Families will say anything.', 'I checked behind me', 'Go stand outside.', 'The fault is in thine ears, not me' ('not I').
Ambiguous name: 'I lose to one who calleth Luna nice.' Viewers will hear 'Luna' as a person who is not on the show, not as the moon. The joke breaks on first hearing.
Stock romance and pickup openings used as setups: 'is this seat taken?', 'Thou art a rose.' Both turn, so they stay, but the rose is the better use of the trick.
Too nice for a star: not applicable. This bank has no star reactions or cuts.
biggestGap: The rhythm is the writer's, not Quill's: 26 lines end on the same clipped stand-up button after a full stop ('He also doeth hair.', 'Any horse.', 'Ask it.', 'Today.'), and the persona's own signature shape, one unbroken overdressed sentence that collapses onto its plain last words, appears in only about six. In the next pass, rewrite the button lines as single run-on florid sentences with no full stop before the turn, as 'Height.' and 'I wish thee' already do, so the cadence alone says Sir Quill.

notes: Files read: refs/writing/monster-prom-lines.md in full, including the section on the voices; charm-notes.md, skimmed; CAST.md; the quill persona; all 112 lines of the bank; the type comments in types.ts; round 2 of this critique. I flagged 22 of 112 lines (19.6%), down from 23.2% in round 2 and 48.2% in round 1. A line is flagged if any test catches it. Lines that share a template but turn on something specific (Norman Conquest, the four-hundred-line ode to Pixel, {rival} accepted, the comma duel) are left out of the count. The round 2 fix landed. The giveaway boast is now the engine, and Quill no longer winks: 'finest bucket maker in Kent', 'winced at by a queen', 'took holy orders the morning after my sonnet cycle', 'No soul hath ever summoned me twice. They are overcome, I believe.', '{wins} wins... The other ladies lacked an ear.', '{losses} ladies chose another. Each, I am certain, under duress.', 'chiefly mine', 'of these four I am the most upright'. The closeCold and lose lines are strict pentameter, and 'Then go, and love a knave who rhymes with lunch.' and 'I leave thee, then, to such as cannot scan.' are keepers. The weakest slots are now wingman and roast, which keep reciting a rival's secret from the brief (goats, the old slice, the door) when they should be pitching the rival through Quill's own blindness, as 'I have paid his processing fee. It is processing.' and 'Choose a canal, fair one.' do. Small construction faults: 'Thou art fair as a sedan chair. I shall carry both ends.' can read as calling the star heavy; 'Hush, little sprout, the floor forgiveth thee.' has no clear meaning; 'Grandly... I had moved her that deeply.' says its joke twice and would be stronger ending at 'sonnet cycle'. Also protect: 'O lady of the singing box... I wish thee.', 'Crumb, a tin hearth with a sulking loaf in it, is the only suitor who is also breakfast', 'Remember me, if thou rememberest aught, as tall.', 'Wed, by a parson who hath been dead some years...', 'Madam, thou art the only fish I have ever wished to court and not to eat on Friday', 'Thy face is a little window with a battle in it. Pray, which side are we on?', and 'Prince is truly royal... It is processing.' Verdict margin: ours wins on the best 12 only. If the button cadence spreads further or the wingman slots stay generic, a full-episode viewing would hand it back to the bar.
